answer: Put the `space-lua` block inside a comment: a commented-out block isn't indexed and the pages read at boot ([[CONFIG]], libraries) skip it, so the script stays off. Note that it is still linted for syntax errors, and `${...}` expressions or Lua-registered code widgets inside a comment still run in the open editor.

--- Markdown/Comment.md ---
Use cases | Scripts stay off
A `space-lua` or `space-style` block inside a comment is _not_ indexed, and the pages read at boot ([[CONFIG]], [[Library|libraries]]) skip it as well, so commenting a script out is how you disable it.

What a comment does not switch off is live evaluation in the open editor: `${...}` [[Space Lua#Expressions|expressions]] and Lua-registered [[API/codeWidget|code widgets]] inside a comment still run and render, and a commented-out `space-lua` block is still linted for syntax errors.

--- CHANGELOG.md ---
CHANGELOG | Edge > 2.11.0
* [[Space Lua]]: scripts that runs too long no longer freeze the editor: after a couple of seconds it offers to stop the script, while the rest of the app stays responsive.
* Fix: Space Lua patterns no longer mistake some non-ASCII characters for ASCII punctuation, which could corrupt page names in `string.gsub` or produce false matches.
* Fix: releasing a drag-selection on top of a link no longer navigates to it — only a real click (pointer down and up in the same spot) follows a link.
* Fix: on Safari/WebKit, selecting a word in a wrapped paragraph could highlight the entire visual line even though only the word was selected.
* Fix: a markdown table whose column happens to be named `ref`, `tag`, `tags`, `itags`, `page` or `tableref` no longer overwrites the indexed row’s own identity.

--- CLI.md ---
Installation | Or pipe from stdin:
echo 'local x = 40; return x + 2' | sb lua

sb lua 'system.reboot()'       # after changing files outside sb (not needed after sb fs write/edit)
sb lua 'space.lint("Page")'    # problems on a page; space.lint() checks every page
```

To check a page without opening it in the editor, call [[API/space#space.lint]]: it runs the editor’s linters (frontmatter and data block YAML, `space-lua` syntax, objects checked against tag schemas, anchors) and renders every `${…}` directive and Lua code widget, returning a list of `{page, line, column, severity, message, source}` for the ones that fail. An empty list means no problems. A page written with `sb fs write` or `sb fs edit` (or through the [[MCP]]) has its scripts reloaded already, so `space.lint` sees them. Only after changing files by other means do you need `sb lua 'system.reboot()'` first.

--- API/system.md ---
system | system.cleanDatabases > system.loadScripts
`system.loadScripts()`

Reloads Space Lua scripts and configuration.

--- CHANGELOG.md ---
CHANGELOG | Edge
* Fix: while Space Lua scripts reloaded (after editing a script page), widgets on the open page could briefly fail with errors such as "attempt to index a nil value", because they rendered against a half-loaded environment. Scripts now load into a fresh environment that takes over only once all of them have run.
* Fix: index-backed views no longer refresh halfway through a queued reindex, which could temporarily hide the page being edited.
* Fix: Git sync errors caused by unrelated histories now offer a recovery action to check and combine both histories. Automatic revisions created during the connection check no longer invalidate it.
